question.text: A block of mass 5 kg sits on a horizontal table. A pulley is fixed at each edge of the table, one on the left and one on the right. A string from the block goes left over the left pulley and down to a hanging block of mass 15 kg; call its tension T₂. Another string from the block goes right over the right pulley and down to a hanging block of mass 5 kg; call its tension T₁. The coefficient of friction between the table and the 5 kg block on it is 0.2. What is the ratio T₁ : T₂ (tension in the right string to tension in the left string)?
conditions: coefficient of friction between the 5 kg block and the table is 0.2
5 kg block sits on the table, connected by strings over pulleys at each edge
left string (T₂) hangs a 15 kg block
right string (T₁) hangs a 5 kg block

figure.description: A block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal table. A pulley sits fixed at the left edge of the table and another at the right edge. The string on the left, labeled T₂, runs from the block over the left pulley and down to a hanging 15 kg block. The string on the right, labeled T₁, runs from the block over the right pulley and down to a hanging 5 kg block.

solution.approach: Write Newton's second law for all three blocks with one common acceleration, include friction on the table block, and solve the three equations together.

steps.text: The 15 kg block is heavier than the 5 kg block, so the system accelerates with the 15 kg block going down, the table block sliding toward the left pulley, and the 5 kg block on the right going up. Call this common acceleration a.
steps.equation: a is the same size for all three blocks

steps.text: Write Newton's second law for the 15 kg block (falling) and the 5 kg block (rising).
Write Newton's second law for the table block. Friction opposes its leftward slide, so it acts to the right; its size is the coefficient of friction times the block's own weight.
Substitute the first two equations into the third and solve for a, then get T₁ and T₂.
The ratio of the right tension to the left tension is T₁ to T₂.

common_mistakes.text: Treating the system as staying at rest and setting each tension equal to the weight it holds gives T₁ = 50 N and T₂ = 150 N, a ratio of 1 : 3.
Leaving out friction on the table block and solving the same three equations with μ = 0 gives T₁ = 70 N and T₂ = 90 N, a ratio of 7 : 9.
